svg.data-input-voltage: 100-240 VAC 50/60 Hz, or -24 to -60 VDC wide range
svg.data-psu-redundancy: two hot-swappable supply bays; the base ships one AC supply and a blank
svg.data-operating-temp: AC system -20 to 65 C; DC system -40 to 65 C
svg.data-services: MPLS L2/L3 VPN, VPWS, VPLS, H-VPLS, 802.1Q, 802.1ad
svg.data-resiliency: G.8031, sub-50 ms G.8032v2 R-APS and MSTP fast ring, sub-50 ms RSVP-TE FRR, H-VPLS dual homing, LAG
svg.data-timing: SyncE, IEEE 1588v2 PTP, BITS and phase clock
svg.data-multicast: IGMP snooping v1/v2/v3, IGMP proxy, MVR
svg.data-local: CON serial console and ETH out-of-band Ethernet on RJ45; DA-15 alarm inputs and outputs
svg.data-mgmt-protocols: Console, Telnet, SSHv2, RADIUS, TACACS+, SNMP v1/2/3, xFTP, NTP, DHCP, NAT, ZTP
svg.data-safety: C-UL 60950, CSA 22.2 No. 950, EN/IEC 60950, TUV/GS, CB, EN 60825-1/2 (2016 edition)

The stencil's shell is ambiguous between the two (24.1 wide, screws 28.4 apart)."},"chassis":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"1.5RU, 440 x 66.3 x 253. Width and depth are the data sheets' (\"440mm (19' racks) x 67mm (2.625') x 253mm (10')\"); the height is not - see chassis-height."},"chassis-height":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"66.3, NOT the data sheet's 67. The height is 440 divided by the rendered face's MEASURED aspect, 6.64 - the render's four corners fix that ratio, and the stencil's body (441.4 x 66.2) agrees with it - against the data sheet's 67; the 0.7 mm between them is recorded rather than split."},"controls":{"confidence":"estimated","note":"The Alarm Cut Off push button is drawn with common/reset-button@1, the nearest library part; the real button is a small square cap about 5 x 7 mm (render and stencil). Reset is a pinhole."},"dc-feed":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"The four-pole green connector at the left end, legend -48VA RETA -48VB RETB, is on the chassis in both the AC and DC stencil masters and in the render (an AC build), so it is drawn on every configuration. The DC system is ordered \"with DC feed connector\"."},"eth-speed":{"confidence":"borrowed","note":"BORROWED, NOT STATED. No edition gives the ETH management port's rate. 1g is taken from the TM-8104's OOB port - same vendor, same OS family and the same console-plus- Ethernet management stack - following the maintainer's ruling for unstated management rates; NetBox's community entry types the 8104's port 1000base-t, itself unsourced. The eth-speed gap stays open."},"fan-tray":{"confidence":"estimated","note":"The data sheets ship a fan tray with every base system. The stencil draws it as a full-height module at the right end (40.85 x 64.66) with two corner thumbscrews and a pull window; the render shows the same. Its bay uses the stencil's position."},"front-layout":{"confidence":"estimated","note":"TWO SOURCES THAT DISAGREE, EACH USED FOR WHAT IT DOES WELL. Positions are read off the 2025 render rectified by a four-corner homography onto the face (corners TL 83.5,155 TR 784.5,154.5 BR 784.5,260.5 BL 84.5,260.5; about 1.6 px/mm, so good to about a millimetre), then scaled 440/441.4 to the data sheet's body. Shapes, pitches and the legends come from the 2022 stencil master, which is AN OLDER BUILD: its supply bays, DA-15 and expansion-slot left edge agree with the render within 2.5 mm, but it draws the SFP blocks 6.8 mm further right, the CON/ETH stack 4 mm right and a different expansion card. Where they disagree on position the render - the current product - is used (see the stencil-vs-render gap)."},"jack-orientation":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"The ETH jack's lamp labels (LNK/ACT, MNG) are printed under it and its lamp windows sit on its lower corners in the render, so it is keyway-down (unrotated); CON above it is turned 180, belly to belly. CON carries no lamps, so the unlamped std/rj45-ganged@2 is used for it."},"lamps":{"confidence":"estimated","note":"TWO ARROW LAMPS PER PORT. Each column carries two \u25b2\u25bc pairs in the strip between the rows - the stencil draws them at 1.55, 4.12, 7.88 and 10.46 mm from the column's left edge, and the render shows the same doubled pattern - so each port has two lamps (-a and -b), up-arrows for the upper port, down for the lower. What the two mean (likely link and activity) is not documented. Sync and Fan are round lamps and Reset a pinhole beside the DA-15; STS and EXT are small lamps over the CON/ETH stack."},"model":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"TM-7124S data sheet (telco.com 2025/12, product page tm-7124); the 2016-08 and 2019-01 editions call it the T-Metro 7124S, which the face prints."},"ports":{"confidence":"estimated","note":"24 std/sfp@1 in three 2 x 4 blocks. The blocks start where the render puts them (x 190.0, 251.8, 313.5 before scaling); inside a block the columns are on the stencil's 14.72 pitch - individual cages with a 0.8 mm web, not a ganged block - which the render's block widths (57.6-58.9 for four columns) corroborate. Rows at y 10.85 and 26.35 (render centres); the lower row is turned 180. Numbered as printed, \"\u25b31 \u25bd2\" over each column: the odd port above, the even below; \"1/\" before each block."},"power":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"NOT STATED: no edition gives a consumption figure.
